items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: I remember in Japan a man coming up to Joe with a whole album of things about Hank Jones that we were talking about, he had Hank’s whole history, all his records

ctx.x: Can you give me an idea of what the English audience was like for jazz music when you first were going back and forth.

Very enthusiastic. Very enthusiastic, and also in Japan, very enthusiastic. In fact, the jazz artists who have been there say they’re better known in these other countries than in the United States. And I remember in Japan a man coming up to Joe with a whole album of things about Hank Jones that we were talking about, he had Hank’s whole history, all his records, he had all Joe’s stuff, he had all Sweets’ stuff. And this is a man in Japanese, a gentleman in Japan. And you know that would be rare here I think.…
